prompts.text: What do you learn about a relative from the way they treat somebody who cannot do anything for them?
A family member changes their name. How would you help the rest of us get used to using it?
Tell us about a family disagreement where discovering one missing fact changed the whole conversation.
Which relative would you ask to help you write a difficult message, and why?
Make a joint decision through a group discussion or hear each person's view privately first?
Somebody often becomes the family messenger without choosing the job. How do we make sure news reaches people directly?
How do you tell the difference between somebody being private and somebody feeling left out?
Living nearby does not automatically make someone responsible for every family errand. How should we share the load?
Which relative has taught you the value of doing a job at a slower pace?
Two households in our family have different rules for children. What should visitors ask before offering advice?
What kind of update would you like to receive directly rather than through another relative?
Describe a moment when a relative defended your right to choose without agreeing with your choice.
Who do you enjoy celebrating for a small achievement other people might overlook?
Ask how a decision feels or ask what practical help would make it easier?
What have you learnt from a relative who does not share your faith or beliefs?
An offer to host sometimes becomes an expectation to host forever. How would we notice when somebody wants a break?
An older relative asks a younger one for help with a phone, then worries about being a nuisance. What response would feel reassuring?
What makes a family introduction feel warm without sharing too much about the person?
Tell us about a time you discovered a relative was nervous about something you assumed they found easy.
Which relative has influenced how you treat people outside the family?
Trying to be fair does not always mean treating every relative identically. What difference in needs do you wish we understood better?
What would you like us to stop assuming about the amount of free time you have?
A relative shares a view in a group chat which seems unlike them. How would you check whether you understood it properly?
How do you like people to acknowledge a favour after you have helped them?
Offer a relative two ways to help or ask them to name a task they would willingly take on?
What helps you trust a relative with an unfinished idea?
Describe a time an unfamiliar family member became familiar through regular brief encounters.
Which relative has surprised you by remembering someone else's important date?
We often know who keeps the family running but rarely ask what support they need. Who should we ask today?
A family member brings a dietary restriction we have never catered for. What would you ask before planning their meal?
Which relative would you like to hear explain a decision you once found puzzling?
Which relative is good at turning a practical question into a conversation you did not expect?
Receive a check-in before a stressful appointment or have someone call after it is over?
What do you pick up from a relative's gestures which you might miss over the phone?
Tell us about a moment when two relatives quietly worked together without needing anyone to direct them.
Somebody wants to share a family photograph publicly, but one person prefers to stay offline. How would we include everyone in the decision?
Who in the family gives praise you find easy to believe?
A family member does not have to turn every skill into a service for everyone. How do we respect a hobby they want to keep personal?
How have your conversations with cousins changed since you stopped seeing one another through school holidays?
What do you wish people understood about your relationship with a relative they find difficult?
Our youngest relatives see adults in roles we barely notice anymore. What have they noticed about us?
We disagree about whether a family occasion should be small or open to everyone. What should we decide before making a guest list?
Describe a time someone from outside the family helped you appreciate a relative's kindness.
Which relative would you trust to tell you when you have misunderstood somebody?
Share one concern before a family trip or agree on a way to raise concerns during it?
How do you prefer us to respond when a plan you were proud of does not work out?
A repeated compliment sometimes turns into pressure to stay the same. Has a label ever felt limiting to you?
What would you like a relative to ask before signing you up for an activity on your behalf?
A family member returns from abroad and everyone asks for gifts before asking about their life. How would you change the welcome?
Which relative would you like to hear speak about something other than their usual area of expertise?
Tell us about an unexpected bond between two relatives who rarely meet.
What do you appreciate about a relative's partner which has nothing to do with how well they fit our routines?
Some relatives keep photographs, while others remember names or dates. How do these different kinds of remembering help us understand one another?
Ask a relative to explain a joke you missed or ask them to tell you what made it funny at the time?
Who would you ask for an honest account of how you behave when you are tired?
A relative has moved into their own home and wants to set new visiting routines. Which details should we ask them to choose?
Which part of a relative's personality becomes clearer when they teach somebody?
Describe a time a relative's short answer made sense once you heard what their day had involved.
What helps relatives of different ages enjoy a conversation without turning it into a lesson?
Checking whether help is wanted takes less effort than repairing resentment later. What sort of help should always start with a question?
Which relative notices when somebody else deserves credit?
Our family collects contributions for a gift, and some people want to give less. How would you keep their choices private?
Discuss an awkward subject while doing something side by side or sit down with no other activity?
Who in the family has helped you take somebody else's worries seriously?
The relative everyone calls dependable sometimes needs permission to be uncertain. How do we make room for their questions?
Tell us about seeing a relative refuse an advantage because it would have been unfair to someone else.
What do you like about a relative's way of bringing a conversation to an end?
A sibling says they would like a relationship which involves more than sorting out family tasks. What might you suggest doing together?
How do we know whether advice from an elder reflects a preference or a firm expectation?
Hear why a relative enjoys solitude or ask what makes company feel worthwhile to them?
Which relative would you invite to explain a family custom to a newcomer, and why?
Being proud of a relative need not turn into speaking on their behalf. When should we let them tell their own story?
Describe a family relationship which became easier when you stopped expecting identical reactions.
What would help us ask about your progress without making you feel we are checking a deadline?
A relative tells the same story twice during a visit. How would you work out whether they want company, an answer or simply an audience?
Which relative has shown you a useful way to accept a compliment?
Some family members ask for help indirectly because a direct request feels awkward. What signals do you notice?
Choose a family activity nobody has tried or let somebody introduce an activity they already love?
What helps you stay close to a sibling whose daily life differs from yours?
Two relatives volunteer for the same task and both want to take charge. What would you ask before dividing the work?
Tell us about a time a relative changed their approach after listening to you.
Who in the family asks newcomers about interests before asking about their job?
A family discussion does not need an agreed conclusion to feel worthwhile. What makes a difference of opinion worth hearing?
Which relative would you ask to accompany you to an important conversation, and what support would you want from them?
A young adult in our family asks to handle a situation themselves. How would we stay available without taking control?
What helps you enjoy a relative's success without comparing your own progress?
Receive encouragement privately or hear someone praise your effort in front of the family?
An unfinished conversation sometimes needs an invitation rather than a reminder. How would you invite someone to return to it?
Describe a time a relative noticed you had become better at something you found difficult.
Which relative do you enjoy watching meet new people?
Our family wants to check in on someone having a busy week. How would we coordinate without overwhelming their phone?
What do you wish we noticed about the effort behind something you make look easy?
Including a relative means asking what participation suits them rather than deciding for them. Where do we get this right?
Talk through a disagreement on the day or agree on a specific time after everyone has rested?
Ask a relative to challenge your assumptions or ask them to help you explain your view more clearly?
What difference in the way two relatives show loyalty have you found interesting?
We want to visit a relative who has a new baby. What should we ask before deciding when to arrive and how long to stay?
Whose opinion do you seek when you want a fresh perspective rather than agreement?
Some relatives use affectionate language while others prefer a straightforward greeting. How do we learn what feels right for each person?
Which family discussion would benefit from hearing the youngest person's view before anyone else speaks?
